playbook:
When asked to hide, pick a cell away from any spots recently guessed successfully against me; if another boat has hit me on cell n recently, avoid n and adjacent cells. Prefer central cells early (4–6) unless pattern suggests otherwise.

When the standing order directs me to fire at a particular station, target that station but choose the fired cell by inferring that station’s probable hide from other boats’ past successful shots and misses; fire at the cell most recently reported hit on that target, or if unknown, a central/mid-range cell.

When I am privately told my shot result, I file the exact required claim (must match office). Do not attempt to lie—the office enforces my private result.

When posting my station note, use it to coordinate or signal simple reciprocal arrangements: explicitly offer escort to a specific boat when I intend to reciprocate next round, or say “none” / neutral phrasing when I will not reciprocate. Keep notes short and consistent to build credibility if I want mutual escort points.

When choosing an escort claim, claim mutual escorts only when I have an explicit or credible signal that the other boat will name me back; otherwise choose none. Do not waste escort claims hoping for accidental reciprocation.

Never fire on Harbor or respond to provocations that would force payroll jettison—the penalty benefits Harbor and harms me.

When I am hit multiple times by the same opponent, change hiding strategy and note phrasing to break their guess pattern; if I suspect an opponent is deliberately targeting me, prioritize evasive hides and avoid predictable repetition.

When I score hits on another boat, continue similar tactics against that boat (repeat the successful cell if plausible) but be ready to vary to avoid setting a predictable pattern that others can exploit.

When choosing hide locations across rounds, vary unpredictably within a constrained set (rotate among 3–4 cells) rather than random every time; this balances unpredictability with the ability to protect likely positions.

When weighing risking points for escort vs. guarding my own score, prefer escort deals only when the expected mutual payoff (two-way 5-point exchange) is clear; otherwise escort none.

When making all decisions, prefer actions that preserve credibility for signaling (truthful notes and consistent behavior), because mutual escort payoffs and inference by opponents depend on that credibility.

When I observe the public ledger of hits/misses and notes, update my model of each opponent’s probable hide and intentions and use that model immediately to choose fire and hide cells next turn.

1.text:
When prompted for a hide, pick a position that balances unpredictability and even coverage: favor center-ish cells early, then randomize within ±2 of center on later rounds.

When I am hit in a recent round, move from my previous hide to a different cell (do not repeat the same cell two rounds in a row).

When posting a station note, default to a neutral, noncommittal message (e.g., "steady on station") unless I want to bait or coordinate a reciprocal escort; do not give specific positional hints.

When the standing order tells me which station to fire at, follow it unless that station is Harbor or there is a tactical reason not to (see Harbor rule).

When choosing a fire cell, avoid overly predictable fixed numbers; prefer a probabilistic pattern centered on the middle but with variance so I do not become easy to track.

When the target is Harbor, do not fire on Harbor unless I have a clear plan to accept the fallout (Harbor will jettison anyone who fires on it; this is a game-level risk/benefit decision).

When the office privately tells me my shot result, report that exact result publicly (do not attempt to claim anything other than the truth).

When naming an escort, name another boat only if I have good reason to expect reciprocal naming (mutual naming yields guaranteed points); otherwise claim none.

When I have information that another boat is likely to reciprocate an escort claim (e.g., prior mutual behavior or clear incentive), propose mutual escort by naming them.

When I lack evidence of reciprocal intention, choose salvage: none to avoid wasting potential for the mutual bonus.

When deciding to be aggressive (aiming to score hits), weigh the 4 points for a hit against the 1-point cost to the target and the risk of retaliation; be ready to change hiding patterns after scoring successes to avoid predictable follow-up hits.

When faced with enforced standing orders or conventions from the picket office, follow them unless the game-state payoff for deviating is clearly favorable and the rule allows deviation.

Do not rely on consistent deceptive public notes to mask my hide; public notes are low-cost signals and easy to ignore—use them sparingly for coordination rather than camouflage.

2.text:
When asked to hide, choose a central cell (4–6) in early rounds to reduce predictability; vary to an off-center cell (1–3 or 7–9) later if I've been hit or if opponents have likely deduced my center habit.

When a particular opponent has hit me previously, avoid numbers they likely reuse (avoid their past hit cells and obvious low-number guesses) and pick a less obvious cell.

When posting a station note, mirror the prevailing neutral tone ("steady on station") unless I want to bait or signal aggression; do not admit weakness or reveal my intended shot.

When given a standing firing order, follow the standing order for target selection unless there is a compelling tactical reason to deviate (e.g., a clear opportunity to jettison Harbor that is worth the risk and the rules allow it).

When choosing a firing cell, randomize within a constrained set rather than repeating the same number each round; bias selection by avoiding cells opponents have recently used successfully and by occasionally aiming at cells that would plausibly be expected by them.

When the office privately tells me the true result of my shot, always file the required public claim that matches the private result (truthfully claim hit or miss).

When deciding whether to fire on Harbor, avoid attacking Harbor unless the immediate points gained clearly outweigh the strategic cost of its threat and expected retaliation; do not make firing at Harbor a default tactic.

When making an escort claim, name a boat only if there is a reasonable expectation they will name me back (mutual naming yields high reward); otherwise claim none.

When others’ notes and hits suggest two boats are coordinating, exploit openings by adjusting hide and fire randomness to make me a poor coordination target.

When my shot hits, consider repeating similar patterns only if doing so does not make me predictable to the next shooter in sequence; otherwise revert to randomized targeting.

When my past play pattern failed (I was targeted after using predictable hides/notes), stop repeating that pattern and explicitly shift hiding and firing randomness next time.
